review: 701.7b-1: grumgully_theirs flipped the outcome through Grumgully's 'you control' condition, not through the continuous effect 701.7b orders; replaced it with no_march, which removes the type-changing effect so the entering replacement no longer sees a creature.

scenarios.title: A token-creating spell puts the specified tokens onto the battlefield

setup.notes: Both libraries are non-empty and irrelevant.

decisions: A casts Raise the Alarm, tapping both Plains.
Both players pass; Raise the Alarm resolves.

variants.label: resolves
variants.expected: Two 1/1 white Soldier creature tokens enter the battlefield under A's control. Raise the Alarm is in A's graveyard.

variants.label: countered
variants.delta: Instead of passing, B responds by casting Counterspell targeting Raise the Alarm, tapping both Islands.
variants.expected: Raise the Alarm is countered and moves to A's graveyard. No tokens are created.

scenarios.title: A replacement effect on a token entering applies after continuous effects have modified the token

setup.notes: March of the Machines makes each noncreature artifact an artifact creature with power and toughness equal to its mana value. A Treasure token has mana value 0. Both libraries are non-empty and irrelevant.

decisions: A casts Strike It Rich, tapping Mountain.
Both players pass; Strike It Rich resolves and creates a Treasure token.

variants.label: grumgully_yours
variants.expected: The Treasure token is already an artifact creature (from March of the Machines) when it enters, so Grumgully's replacement gives it an additional +1/+1 counter: it enters as a 1/1 artifact creature with one +1/+1 counter and stays on the battlefield.

variants.label: no_march
variants.delta: March of the Machines is not on the battlefield.
variants.expected: The Treasure token enters as a noncreature artifact with no +1/+1 counter and stays on the battlefield.

scenarios.forge_notes: The token must be seen as a creature by the entering replacement; confirm Forge applies the static type change to the token before evaluating the ETBReplacement.

scenarios.title: A replacement effect on token creation applies before continuous effects modify the token

setup.notes: Divine Visitation: if one or more creature tokens would be created under your control, that many 4/4 white Angel creature tokens with flying and vigilance are created instead. March of the Machines makes a Treasure token (mana value 0) a 0/0 artifact creature. Both libraries are non-empty and irrelevant.

decisions: A casts Strike It Rich, tapping Mountain.
Both players pass; Strike It Rich resolves and creates a Treasure token.

variants.label: treasure
variants.expected: When the Treasure token is created it is not yet a creature, because March of the Machines is considered afterwards, so Divine Visitation does not replace it: one Treasure token is created. March of the Machines then makes it a 0/0 artifact creature and it is put into the graveyard (ceases to exist) in the next state-based check.

variants.label: soldiers
variants.delta: A casts Raise the Alarm instead of Strike It Rich, tapping both Plains.
variants.expected: The two tokens are creature tokens as created, so Divine Visitation replaces them: two 4/4 white Angel creature tokens with flying and vigilance enter instead of the Soldiers.

scenarios.forge_notes: Confirm Forge evaluates ValidToken$ Creature.YouCtrl on the token before static abilities apply.
